statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Registre des entreprises en ligne (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Quebec business corporation must be in French as required by the Charter of the French Language (C.Q.L.R., c. C-11). The name may include Latin characters, Arabic numerals, punctuation marks and recognized legal suffixes (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée'). A foreign-script business name must be transliterated into Latin characters, and a French version must normally accompany any non-French logo or translation. The name must be distinguishable from existing names in the REQ and must not connote government association, regulated professions, or a misleading business purpose.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a REQ name refusal, the applicant is notified in writing. The applicant may file a written request for administrative reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the refusal, demonstrating that the proposed name is distinguishable and compliant. If the Registraire maintains the refusal, the applicant may either propose an alternative name in a new application or appeal the decision to the Court of Québec (Civil Chamber) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Quebec Code of Civil Procedure. It is advisable to retain legal counsel to prepare a revised name and substantiate the appeal with REQ analytical comparisons.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a duly licensed virtual office or registered agent providing a physical street address in Quebec; a post-office box alone is prohibited. For the ISIC 7420 stock photography and generative visual assets business, a virtual office is acceptable for the registered office and statutory records, but banks and the Canada Revenue Agency may demand real business substance, operational records, and physical presence indicators before allowing GST/HST registration or merchant account activation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<10%) for a low-risk digital media enterprise; unannounced on-site inspections are rare under Quebec's professional corporations regime. The risk becomes moderately higher if the société uses a virtual office without an actual Quebec business site, or if tax filings and payment processor records are inconsistent with the declared commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, arts. 12 (incorporation), 22-24 (articles), 39 (name), 97-103 (registered office and records); Civil Code of Quebec arts. 296-298
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. The corporation may be incorporated without a minimum stated capital and no escrow or capital-holding account is mandated. Official filing duties are collected by the REQ in CAD and are not denominated in USD.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation does hereby issue to the subscribers identified in the minutes an aggregate of 100 common shares at a price of CAD 1.00 per share, and that the subscription amounts are credited to the corporation's stated capital; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be established at [address], City of Quebec, Province of Quebec, and that corporate records be maintained there or in another location permitted by the Business Corporations Act (Quebec); RESOLVED, that [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed directors of the corporation until the next annual meeting; RESOLVED, that [Officer A] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Officer B] Secretary, and [Officer C] Chief Financial Officer, each to hold office until successors are elected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online name-search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-search request through the REQ portal using the Acces services electronic platform. The proposed name must contain a distinguishing element, a descriptive element and a legal ending such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.', and must comply with the Charter of the French Language. Retain the name-search decision and file number for use in the articles. No notarization is required for this stage.
required_dossiers: Consent documents, if the proposed name contains regulated words
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the REQ will state the reasons in its decision. The applicant may immediately file a new name-search request with a compliant alternative; there is no restrictive appeal right against a name refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary (for drafting) and REQ electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft articles of incorporation containing the corporate name, share structure, any restrictions on share transfers, the number of directors, and the initial registered office address. Each incorporator must execute the articles. Identify the first directors in the accompanying declaration. If the articles are submitted electronically, a valid REQ access code or digital signature authorization is required.
required_dossiers: Drafted and executed articles of incorporation
Minutes of the incorporator, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ objects to the content of the articles, the applicant must amend and resubmit the articles using the same file number within the period indicated in the deficiency notice. Substantive corrections may require a new execution of the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with the Registraire des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Registraire central des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the finalized articles through the REQ electronic deposit service, pay the applicable CAD duty, and request issuance of the certificate of constitution and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). After verification, the REQ registers the corporation and issues the attestation of constitution. Verify the registered office address and director information before confirming the filing.
required_dossiers: Articles of incorporation in final form
Registered office address, including municipal and postal address
List of first directors and their signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the REQ issues a notice identifying defects. Correctable defects are remedied by filing an amending declaration or amended articles. Non-correctable defects require a new application. A substantive refusal may be appealed to the Court of Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; Revenu Quebec; Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting and adopt the first board resolutions and by-laws. Issue share certificates, open the corporate bank account, and prepare the minute book. Register with Revenu Quebec for GST, QST, and Quebec pension and parental insurance plan obligations if applicable, and with the Canada Revenue Agency for a business number, if required. Maintain books and records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and organizational minutes
Revenu Quebec registration forms and CRA business number application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration with Revenu Quebec or the CRA may attract penalties and interest. Submit the relevant registration declarations online within 30 days of receiving a notice, and file any amendments to the articles or director information with the REQ.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE) - no industrial permit is applicable to a purely digital stock-photo and generative visual assets platform
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - Quebec law imposes no sectoral operating or manufacturing permit for the online commercial distribution of photographic and AI-generated visual content

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical production, laboratory, manufacturing facility, or generating asset; no environmental impact assessment or attestation is required under the Quebec Environment Quality Act or the federal Impact Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the business generates no wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. Any leased office space must comply with municipal fire, electrical, and waste disposal by-laws and with the Quebec Building Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a pure e-commerce and digital content platform; if a physical office or content studio is leased, obtain a municipal fire safety certificate, complete structural occupancy compliance under the Quebec Building Code, and register with the Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST) if the corporation has employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (federal GST/HST, corporate income tax and Business Number administration); Revenu Québec (Quebec Sales Tax, provincial corporate income tax, payroll and consumption taxes). Electronic portals: CRA My Business Account / Mon dossier d'entreprise and Revenu Québec Mon dossier d'entreprise via CléNumérique.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation first registers for a federal Business Number (BN) with a program account using Business Registration Online, Form RC1-W or a CRA application; the BN is a 9-digit number with a two-letter account code (RT for GST/HST, RC for corporate income tax). For Quebec, the entity must separately register with Revenu Québec for QST via the Register a Business service or Form LM-1-V and will receive a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Registration is mandatory once the small-supplier threshold is exceeded or if the non-resident elects to register voluntarily; the same BN is used for all federal accounts and QST filings, and Revenu Québec may accept the BN as the common registrant identifier after NEQ issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A business corporation incorporated federally or in Quebec is a legally separate taxable entity; it is not fiscally transparent and cannot be treated as a disregarded entity. As a resident corporation (by place of incorporation or central management and control), it is subject to Canadian income tax on worldwide income, while a non-resident corporation is taxed only on Canadian-source income and can be subject to branch tax under Income Tax Act section 219.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian tax law; corporations are statutorily taxable entities. Available elections relevant to cross-border digital asset platforms include: (i) Income Tax Act section 216(1) net-basis election for non-residents earning Canadian rental or certain Canadian-source income, (ii) the non-resident corporation election to file a Part I return instead of Part XIII withholding where treaty or statute permits, (iii) GST/HST registrant elections for closely related corporations and joint election for employer-employee rebates, and (iv) hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act (sections 18.6 to 18.8 as enacted following BEPS Action 2) which disallow deductions where a hybrid entity or instrument creates a cross-border double non-taxation outcome.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST under the Excise Tax Act) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST / Taxe de vente du Québec administered by Revenu Québec). Quebec does not participate in the federal HST; the combined consumer incidence is 5% GST plus 9.975% QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small-supplier threshold): a supplier must register for GST/HST once total worldwide taxable supplies from Canadian economic activity exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (Excise Tax Act sections 148 and 240). The same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to QST registration by Revenu Québec under the Taxation Act; registration as a QST registrant is required for any person carrying on commercial activity in Quebec who exceeds the threshold, and voluntary registration is available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing or tax clearance stamping regime is currently in force. CRA and Revenu Québec do not operate continuous transaction control (CTC) reporting; invoicing must comply with the Excise Tax Act disclosure rules and Quebec's French-language invoice rules. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard, based on the Peppol network, is being adopted voluntarily for B2B electronic exchange but is not a fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate; electronic records supporting GST/HST and QST invoices must be retained for at least six years and made available in a readable format on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: zero-rating applies where tangible personal property is exported in accordance with Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act, with documentary evidence that the goods have been shipped out of Canada and title transferred to the non-resident buyer. For services and intangible personal property, including commercial stock photography licences and generative visual assets: the supply is zero-rated when made to a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST and the service or intangible is not principally for use in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance. The platform must demonstrate that the buyer is outside Canada (billing address, IP geolocation, payment settlement data from Stripe or PayPal) and that the digital asset or licence is delivered offshore; domestic Canadian licences and downloads remain taxable at the combined GST+QST rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13A or Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) for physical exports)
Bill of Lading, air waybill or courier delivery proof evidencing movement out of Canada
Inward remittance certificate or bank/FX transfer record demonstrating receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice / zero-rated tax invoice bearing the GST/HST and QST registration numbers and export statement
Stock photo or generative visual asset licence agreement identifying the non-resident licensee and territorial scope of the intellectual property
Stripe/PayPal settlement records and buyer geolocation metadata substantiating the offshore digital delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec scrutinise export zero-rating through complete export documentation and non-resident status evidence. If goods or digital supplies are not demonstrably exported or retained in Canada, or if invoices are fraudulent, the entire output tax is re-assessed at 5% GST and 9.975% QST with interest from the original due date. Gross negligence penalties may be assessed under Excise Tax Act section 285.1 (generally 20% of the net tax amount), Income Tax Act section 163(2) (50% of tax avoided), and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Excise Tax Act section 327 or Income Tax Act section 239, carrying substantial fines and imprisonment. The normal four-year GST/HST and QST reassessment window is extended without limit for misrepresentation, fraud or wilful default, permitting retrospective clawbacks of refunds previously granted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority for CAD; foreign-exchange policy administration rests with the Department of Finance Canada; prudential supervision of banks is delegated to OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions); cross-border transaction monitoring and AML reporting are administered by FINTRAC and the Canada Border Services Agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII status. There are no exchange controls, no Central Bank approval gates, and no repatriation licensing requirements for inward capital injections, profit remittances, dividend payments, or royalty outflows. The functional currency for accounting may be CAD or USD; Quebec corporate tax filings require CAD-denominated financial statements under IFRS/IAS 21. The only material statutory friction on profit outbound is Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory rate, treaty-reduced), which is a tax compliance matter rather than an FX convertibility hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline for export-proceeds repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio (surrender requirement is 0%). Export receipts from stock-photo license sales and AI-generated visual asset subscriptions may be retained indefinitely in USD or other foreign currencies in Canadian or offshore accounts. For GST/HST purposes, export sales of digital photographic assets are zero-rated supplies; the exporter must retain documentation of non-resident customers to support the zero-rating. FINTRAC large-cross-border-transaction reporting applies to fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and CAD 10,000 or more in cash must be reported by the bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational CAD Account plus pooled USD account; capital escrow/trust account available

Operational account in CAD with treasury sweeps; capital reserve account
Operational account and Foreign Currency Account (USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a payment-orchestration layer, not as a substitute for a regulated tier-1 bank account. Canada does not operate an EU-style EMI licence framework. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Airwallex, and Payoneer can provide multi-currency accounts via pooled partner-bank arrangements and are useful for mass low-value disbursements to photographers and micro-suppliers, but they are not CDIC-insured, are not direct members of the Canadian clearing system, and cannot accept deposits in the legal sense. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), payment service providers offering services to Canadians must register with the Bank of Canada; foreign EMIs that merely route funds into Canada generally operate under limited exemptions and remain under the AML supervision of FINTRAC. The recommended treasury architecture is a tier-1 Quebec bank account as the treasury spine, with EMIs and platform payout rails (Stripe Connect and PayPal) used as disbursement conduits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch appearance is not a statutory mandate under Canadian federal AML/ATF rules. FINTRAC-compliant remote onboarding using electronic identity verification, video-conference confirmation, and digital/notarized identity documents is permissible provided the bank has no doubt about the identity of directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners. In practice, Quebec banks often require an initial in-person or video meeting when a newly incorporated entity has non-resident directors or complex UBO structures. Remote opening is generally available where all directors and signatories are Canadian residents with valid government-issued ID; non-resident directors can usually satisfy KYC through a notarized passport copy plus a video call, but the bank reserves discretionary authority to require attendance at a Montreal or Quebec City branch for enhanced due diligence cases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or UBOs without a Canadian banking footprint or Canadian-issued identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports for all directors, officers, and UBOs; Quebec Registraire des entreprises certificate of incumbency and beneficial-owner attestation; corporate organizational chart; proof of residence for each individual; board resolution authorizing account opening; professional reference letter from a licensed Canadian accountant or lawyer

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered office (often a registered-agent or law-firm address) and the actual operational location
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease or sublease agreement; virtual-office service contract; QST/GST registration certificate; corporate website, product documentation, and operational evidence demonstrating a genuine stock-photo platform; explanation of remote-work and outsourced engineering arrangements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound international capital injection structured as share subscription or shareholder loan with unclear source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution approving the capital contribution; executed share-subscription agreement or loan agreement; bank or brokerage statements showing the source and full wire path of the funds; authorizing director identification; audited or reviewed financial statements if available; explanation of the economic substance of the transaction

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening or jurisdiction-risk flags on shareholders, payees, or the AI visual-asset supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions self-declaration; UBO registry demonstrating no shareholders in sanctioned jurisdictions; export-control and content-licensing compliance policy; list of photographer and customer jurisdictions; evidence that the corporate bank account will not receive funds from sanctioned counterparties; FINTRAC political-exposure screening declarations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industrial classification ambiguity compared with higher-risk digital assets, crypto, or NFT platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written business-model description identifying the entity as a stock-photography and generative-visual-assets marketplace under NAICS 541922; proof that no crypto-asset brokerage or unregulated money-service activity is conducted; FINTRAC MSB registration status if applicable; financial projections demonstrating ordinary commercial sales; bank references from existing payment processors

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity or shareholder-loan proceeds via SWIFT MT103 with clear remittance narrative stating Share Capital Contribution or Shareholder Subordinated Loan. For CAD settlement use the Canadian Lynx real-time gross settlement system; for USD leg use Fedwire or CHIPS through the receiving bank. The remittance narrative should reference the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the corporate legal name to satisfy FATCA/CRS classification. No official purpose-code taxonomy applies in Canada; however the bank will require a source-of-funds declaration and will report any transaction of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. Deposited funds should first be credited to a capital escrow sub-account and released to the operating account only upon board resolution specifying the capital-allocation purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For royalty and service-fee payments to photographers and content suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 for global payouts, Canada Lynx for domestic CAD EFT, and Fedwire or CHIPS for USD-denominated settlements; commercial letters of credit are inapplicable to digital stock-photo and AI-asset transactions, so disbursing against invoice with contractual payment terms is standard. For mass micropayments, use platform payout rails including Stripe Connect, PayPal MassPay, and Wise Batch. The jurisdiction of each payee must be verified to support income-tax and Part XIII withholding obligations: the statutory rate on non-resident royalties and services is 25%, with Canada-US treaty rates lowered to 10% for most royalties and to 0% for copyright royalties on production or reproduction of artistic and literary works, provided the payee submits a complete NR301 declaration. GST/HST zero-rating documentation must evidence the non-resident recipient status for every outbound disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) up to a tenor of 24 months used to lock conversion rates on committed inbound capital and forecasted subscription revenue
FX swaps for rolling settlement exposure between CAD, USD, and EUR treasury balances
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) used to hedge currency risk on non-resident shareholder loans denominated in foreign currency
OTC FX options, including vanilla European-style contracts, with tenors aligned to expected monthly revenue collection cycles

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible but commercially unnecessary for the CAD/USD pair because CAD is a fully deliverable, convertible currency; NDFs would apply only to exotic emerging-market currency exposure, which is outside the expected business model

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for the corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of CAD 60 (USD 44); failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution by REQ after a penalty notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid federal tax plus 1% per full month of delay, up to 12 months; separate penalty applies for nil-filing late returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid Quebec tax, plus compounded interest; additional administrative penalties for continuous non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, a private corporation may be exempt from appointing an auditor if shareholders unanimously approve the waiver and the corporation meets the small business corporation criteria: annual gross revenue under CAD 1,000,000 and total assets under CAD 500,000. A compulsory audit is triggered if the corporation is a reporting issuer, fails these size thresholds, or a shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting shares demands an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for non-listed enterprises; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for public or reporting issuers.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law requires the annual declaration to REQ to include a current list of shareholders holding 25% or more of the voting shares. Any transfer of effective control or shareholding above 25% must be reported to REQ within 15 days. The register of individuals with significant control must be reviewed and confirmed annually, including details of residential address and percentage of ownership.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 4,000–10,000 (USD 3,000–7,500); nil if audit is waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%). For a Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the small business deduction on eligible active business income, the combined rate is approximately 12.2%; the stock-photo AI platform must assess whether it qualifies under the SBD rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit – 35% refundable on qualified expenditures for Canadian-controlled private corporations, 15% non-refundable for other corporations; Quebec Research and Development Tax Credit – 14% refundable (up to 2027, altered by Quebec tax reform); Quebec Innovation Tax Credit for selected IP; depreciation under Class 50 (100% immediate expensing) for computer software and data infrastructure; provincial tax credits for multimedia and digital animation not generally applicable to stock photography distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via CRA's My Business Account, EFILE, or NETFILE. Quebec: CO-17 Sociétés Income Tax Return filed via Revenu Québec's clic Revenu secure portal. Both returns are due separately; federal and provincial returns are not consolidated.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. The federal balance of tax is due within two months after year-end (three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations, and for most corporations in Quebec the same due-date alignment applies under the Quebec Taxation Act, with Quebec instalments payable monthly).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from stock photography sales, subscription fees, AI-generated visual asset licensing, royalty income, and advertising-related revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations conducting business in Canada must report only Canadian-source income on this line; treaty-based reductions require Schedule 91 and a completed NR301.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital gains from the disposition of intangible property such as photographic libraries, algorithms, and underlying AI models; 50% taxable inclusion rate applies across Canada.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation disposing of Canadian-taxable property must include the taxable capital gain on this line; certification of exemption is made on Form NR301 where a DTA applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-capital loss carryforward applied in computing taxable income from prior years; net capital losses are carried forward indefinitely on a separate schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may deduct non-capital losses only from Canadian-source income; foreign loss usage must be consistent with CRA's non-resident loss attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income earned in Canada by a non-resident corporation from carrying on a business in Canada, including cross-border digital supply through an AI platform where a permanent establishment is held.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report treaty-protected business income on Schedule 91; otherwise Canadian-source business income is fully taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before income taxes, combining all operating income, recurring licence fees, and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident filing Part I under section 115, this line equals net taxable income earned only in Canada, adjusted by Article VII jurisdiction rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic federal income tax before federal abatement and credits, computed at the 15% base corporate rate and adjusted by general rate reduction or small business deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The federal tax base under Part I applies only when the non-resident corporation elects to file a joint return via Part I; otherwise non-resident withholding under Part XIII is the primary mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal income tax payable after adding Manitoba surcharge, provincial abatement (Quebec abatement), and refundable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations receive no provincial abatement unless they file with Revenu Québec as carrying on business through a permanent establishment in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after federal/Quebec harmonization adjustments and incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a Quebec permanent establishment must file CO-17 and pay Quebec income tax on the income allocated to the Quebec establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance, plus 1% per month up to 12 months, and daily compounded interest at CRA's prescribed rate. Quebec late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax, plus an additional 0.5% per month up to 12 months, and interest on arrears; repeated failure to file may result in gross-negligence penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act, including fines up to 50% of the amount avoided.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-resident shareholders; the rate is reduced by Canada's tax treaty network (Canada-US: 15% for portfolio dividend, 5% if the beneficial owner holds 10% or more of the voting shares; Quebec does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced dividend withholding, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete Form NR301 (Treaty-Based Waiver) and provide a valid Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction. The Canadian corporation must retain the NR301 and TRC, apply withheld amounts using the appropriate treaty rate account (CRA Part XIII account), and if the withholding was initially at 25%, the non-resident must file a T108 Part XIII return or a refund claim under section 227(6) within the prescribed limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalty payments to non-residents is 25% under Part XIII; treaty rates vary: Canada-US copyright royalties on literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works are exempt at 0%; other IP royalties (patents, know-how, trademarks) are 10%; arm's-length interest paid to non-residents is subject to 25% statutory withholding but the Canada-US treaty reduces cross-border interest to 0% when the beneficial owner is not exempt under domestic law; Quebec aligns with federal Part XIII and does not levy an additional provincial withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents must be filed when the aggregate value of covered transactions with each non-resident non-arm's-length person exceeds CAD 1,000,000, or when the highest amount of unpaid intercompany debt exceeds CAD 1,000,000. OECD-aligned Local File, Master File, and Country-by-Country Report threshold: CRA expects contemporaneous documentation for entities with total gross revenue or assets exceeding CAD 50,000,000, or where cross-border related-party transactions exceed CAD 5,000,000 for a single transaction class.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply a Gulf-cooperation-type ESR, but the tax authorities enforce substance through the 'central management and control' residence test, General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245, and the Quebec Taxation Act's abuse-of-rights doctrine. A stock-photo AI company must demonstrate real board meetings in Canada, operational decision-making, contracts, payroll, and datacentre/algorithm ownership in Canada; failure to maintain local substance may permit re-characterization as a foreign-resident shell and the denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully reporting less revenue from Canadian stock-photo and AI licencing by channelling payments through non-resident shell accounts, fabricating digital-asset depreciation, misleading declarations, or suppressing SR&ED expenditure documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act, s.239: fine on conviction of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded, plus imprisonment up to five years; court-ordered payment of arrears, interest and penalties; Quebec Taxation Act s.53 imposes additional penalties and provincial fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate income taxes where they signed or participated in wilful evasion; CRA may issue director-liability assessments under s.227.1 for unremitted source deductions and under s.160 for insufficient consideration transfers; travel bans may be issued where a criminal charge is laid or where CRA believes the director is attempting to leave Canada with taxable assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing stock-photo franchise fees, AI data licensing, or corporate guarantee fees to an offshore affiliate below arm's length, or producing documentation after the filing deadline without contemporaneous support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act, s.247(3): 10% penalty on the largest transfer pricing adjustment where the taxpayer did not make reasonable efforts to use arm's length prices; CRA may also invoke GAAR to deny the entire transaction benefit; Quebec imposes additional reassessment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not personally liable for simple transfer pricing reassessments, but where false invoices or fictitious royalties are used, the directors face s.239 tax evasion personal liability, money-laundering charges, and administrative civil penalties for gross negligence under CRA's reporting rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a listed Canadian agent and board of directors who do not actually direct the business; outsourcing all AI licensing decisions, contract negotiation, and data storage to a foreign entity while recording Canadian profits artificially.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can re-characterize the Canadian entity as not 'resident in Canada' and deny treaty relief; GAAR allows cancellation of tax benefits; under the Quebec Companies Act, a reconsideration may lead to dissolution or revocation of authority to carry on business in Quebec.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who sign materially false returns or permit fraudulent invoicing may be assessed civilly under Quebec civil liability principles; CRA may pursue a third-party civil action for conspiracy, and Canadian courts may issue international travel bans under the Tax Court's interlocutory powers where a director fails to provide security for reassessed tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the stock-photo platform to process payment for sanctions-listed parties or failing to register under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act if carrying out money services business activity through foreign-exchange or payout-side transaction accounts; failing to report suspicious electronic royalty payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000; criminal liability for knowingly engaging in prostitution, tax evasion facilitation, or terrorism funding with a fine and imprisonment up to five years; Quebec's Attorney General may seize the corporate bank accounts under provincial civil forfeiture legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve transactions with non-compliant third parties may be personally liable as de facto money transmitters; Canadian courts may impose asset-freeze injunctions, travel bans, and extradition orders for ML-activity, and the company's corporate veil is pierced when the board is found to be a mere façade.
